resale_co.name: Resale Certificate of Inspection / Housing Clear Certificate (certificate of continued occupancy)
resale_co.lead_time: Apply at least 30 business days before closing, as soon as the seller decides to sell. No same-day inspections.
requirements: Ten-year sealed battery smoke alarm on each level of living space, in every bedroom and in the basement
Carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of the sleeping areas
Fire extinguisher 2A-10B:C under 10 lb within 10 feet of the kitchen, visible, not behind a door or cabinet, top no more than 5 feet above the floor
Chimney certification for fossil fuel burning fireplaces and appliances
Handrails on 4 or more risers; guardrails on porches and decks 30 inches or more above grade
GFCI outlets within 6 feet of water; circuit breaker panel in order; no bare-wire fixtures
Ceilings, walls and floors without holes, chipped paint, severe cracks or water stains
Key locks on entry doors only
Heat, appliances, hot and cold water and toilets working; anti-tip device on range
Water heater bonding strap and relief valve pipe extended to 6 inches from the floor
Bathroom has a window or exhaust fan
Utilities on at the time of inspection
Yard free of trash, motor vehicles and debris; no exterior damage or roof leaks; code violations abated
No work without permits, no illegal apartments or illegally rented rooms

resale_co.how_to_apply: Once there is a buyer, the seller or agent submits the Resale Certificate of Inspection Application to resales@burlingtonnj.us (or by mail to Code Enforcement, 525 High Street) with the $100 fee. Pay online through the city's Pay Here link on the Code Enforcement page, using the property address as the reference number. Code Enforcement emails the appointment to the agent; inspections are Monday, Wednesday and Friday 9 AM to 1 PM. A lock box code is used only if the home is vacant.

evidence.quote: Homes that are sold in the City of Burlington must be inspected. The seller must receive a Housing Clear Certificate before transferring ownership.
Property owners who are intending to sell any dwelling unit
This should be done at least 30 business days before closing
A residential certificate of continued occupancy shall be effective for a period of 60 days.
Failure to obtain a certificate and comply with the ordinance of the City of Burlington (Chapter 195, Housing Standards), will be subject to a fine up to $500.
RESALE CERTIFICATE OF INSPECTION APPLICATION $100.00 Fee
Autumn Harley, Resales Tel: 609-386-0200 ext. 132 Email: Resales@burlingtonnj.us

resale_co.notes: Required by City Ordinance Chapter 195 (Housing Standards), section 195-15A; fees under Chapter 146 (146-15). If the home fails, the buyer can take responsibility for the listed items by signing a notarized Affidavit in Lieu to get a temporary housing conditional certificate before settlement; if the report says no occupancy, the temporary certificate is for work only. Certificates are not transferable and fees are not refundable. The certificate is emailed to the agent about 2 to 3 business days after a passed inspection.

requirements: Ten-year sealed battery smoke alarm on each level, in every bedroom and in the basement

Fire extinguisher 2A-10B:C, under 10 lb, within 10 feet of each kitchen, visible and accessible, on the maker's bracket, top no more than 5 feet above the floor (Resale Process dated February 2026 still requires it)

fire_cert.notes: Burlington City is its own fire code enforcing agency (municipal). The Division of Fire Prevention (Fire Official Corey Towner, 609-386-0200 ext. 171, CTowner@burlingtonnj.us) inspects commercial occupancies and runs a smoke detector program for low income and senior housing; the DCA directory lists 'Burlington City Fire Prev' under smoke detector compliance. For home sales, the city's Resale Process says the Code Enforcement resale inspection is the basis for both the Housing Clear Certificate and the NJ Division of Fire Safety certificate, so there is one application and one fee. The city still lists the extinguisher although P.L.2025, c.19 (February 3, 2025) removed it from the state rule.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: All open construction permits must be closed out with the Construction Office, and any work needing permits must pass permit inspection, before the city issues the final clear housing certificate.

other_items.label: Permits for water heaters and HVAC
other_items.detail: The application asks that permits be pulled and closed for all water heaters, HVAC equipment and any other work before the inspection.

other_items.label: Chimney certification
other_items.detail: Needed for fossil fuel burning fireplaces and appliances.
